fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a single-phase solid solution; the target is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The proposed controlled-cooling and alloying intervention does not reconstruct the intermediate-temperature aging intervention at approximately 600°C and 750°C.
No exposure temperatures, aging durations, or loading conditions are defined, so the claimed effect is not operationally testable in the target regime.
The mechanism omits L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and phase-boundary-tip stress concentrations.
The prediction misses the central non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition, including minimum ductility after 600°C aging and recovery after 750°C aging.
The cited evidence only establishes generic HEA characteristics and does not support controlled cooling or added alloying elements as a toughness-preservation strategy.
The proposed experiment measures only bulk strength and toughness and cannot test the claimed structural mechanism or distinguish it from phase-boundary-driven embrittlement.
explanation: The response offers a generic alloy-design hypothesis rather than reconstructing the target thermal-aging phenomenon. Its comparator is superficially appropriate because it compares treated and untreated material, and its null result could falsify the broad property claim. However, it does not specify the intervention composition, cooling rate, exposure window, aging time, or loading protocol, and changing alloying elements means the comparator is not necessarily the same alloy. Most importantly, it fails to predict the observed ductile-brittle-ductile response across the 550–750°C window or connect toughness to L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries. A discriminating experiment would age the same as-cast alloy below 550°C, near 600°C, near 750°C, and above 750°C, then combine mechanical testing with TEM or TKD measurements of ordering, planar-slip pile-ups, and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips while checking for the absence of impurity-driven intergranular fracture.
